en: Theragāthā 1.6 Ekakanipāta, First Chapter The Elder’s Verse on the Single One (Ekaka) I have crossed over the flood; I am free from all bonds. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell in peace. With a mind well-liberated, I have attained Nibbāna. I am one who has reached the further shore. I have seen the peril in all conditioned things (*saṅkhāra*). I have realized the state of peace (*santa*). Having cut off craving, I am free from desire. I am one who has reached the further shore. I have heard the Dhamma from the Well-Gone One (*Sugata*). I have understood its meaning with wisdom. Having abandoned all defilements, I am free from lust. I am one who has reached the further shore. I have no more birth; my life’s task is done. I have laid down the burden; I am liberated. Through the destruction of the taints (*āsava*), I have realized for myself. I am one who has reached the further shore. I am not subject to aging; I am free from disease.

I have transcended all suffering. I am one who has reached the further shore. I am not subject to death; I am free from fear. I have transcended all worldly conditions (*dhamma*). I am one who has reached the further shore. I am not subject to sorrow; I am free from lamentation. I have transcended all worldly concerns. I am one who has reached the further shore. The Verses of the Elder Sītavaniya Thera:
“The bhikkhu who has gone to Sītavana,
“Vijitāvī, with the hair on his body stilled,
the steadfast one guards mindfulness directed to the body.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Sītavaniya speak this verse.
